extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and other practitioners who appear before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order resolving a disciplinary complaint by means of a proposed settlement agreement; sets out jurisdiction, admitted violations, sanctions, publication and notification obligations, and compliance timelines for a (non-registered) attorney authorized to practice non-patent matters before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this proceeding pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3) and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the statutory and regulatory authority for OED to adjudicate and accept settlement of disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code to non-registered attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is an attorney in good standing in the Commonwealth of Virginia and, as such, is an individual authorized under 5 U.S.C. § 500(b) to practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters; hence Respondent is a practitioner subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being non-registered for patent practice does not shield an attorney from USPTO discipline for non-patent matters when authorized under 5 U.S.C. § 500(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: State-bar misconduct findings as basis for USPTO action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Virginia State Bar Disciplinary Board issued Respondent an Admonition with Terms for violating Rules 3.3(a)(1), 4.1(a), 8.1(a), and 8.4(c) of the Virginia Rules of Professional Conduct based upon knowingly making false statements to a tribunal, the Virginia State Bar in connection with a disciplinary matter, and other persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State disciplinary findings and factual predicates (e.g., misconduct in court appearances) can be adopted or relied upon by USPTO OED in its disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) and (b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) for engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation and 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) for engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific regulatory provisions define misconduct categories (dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation; conduct reflecting adversely on fitness) that warrant discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26; it resolves all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement agreement that meets § 11.26 requirements may be submitted to the USPTO Director to voluntarily resolve a disciplinary complaint; the Final Order implements those agreed terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reprimand is an available sanction; the Final Order both imposes the reprimand and directs its publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at: http://des.uspto.gov/FinalOEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders are posted publicly in the OED Reading Room as part of the disciplinary record and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Reprimand in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette: (text of Notice summarizing Respondent's non-registered status, the regulations violated, and the underlying Virginia State Bar admonition and facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice must identify the practitioner, state the violations (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) and (b)(6)), and provide a concise factual summary supporting the reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification requirement (60 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within sixty (60) days from the date of this Final Order, Respondent shall provide a copy of the Final Order to all of Respondent's clients who have trademark applications pending before the Office on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner is required to notify current USPTO clients with pending matters of the Final Order within a specific timeframe (60 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance (75 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall submit an affidavit to the OED Director within seventy-five (75) days from the date the Final Order is signed showing that he timely provided a copy of the Final Order to clients required to be so notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit serves as evidence of compliance with the client-notification obligation and must be submitted within the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED must communicate disciplinary outcomes to other regulatory or judicial bodies and to the public in accordance with § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement specifies that each party is responsible for its own costs related to the matter and its implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Order resolves disciplinary action arising from stipulated facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement ... resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement and Final Order operate to fully resolve the discrete matters described in the stipulated facts; the language frames the scope of the resolution.
